text:
I reviewed all first-party code, packaging, README, tests, and fixtures. The project is small and test coverage is decent: `python -m pytest -q` passes with 61 tests. I also AST-parsed all Python files successfully. `compileall` was blocked only because the mounted workspace could not create `__pycache__`.

Overall score: **6/10**. I would **not approve as-is**. The code is readable and close to usable, but the accounting layer has several data-correctness bugs that can silently produce wrong reports.

| Severity | File | Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| high | `jobwatch/db.py` | 70-84 | Same-rank terminal states overwrite each other without timestamp comparison, so stale dumps can replace newer final job data. |
| high | `jobwatch/db.py` | 74-80 | Re-ingest treats rows as unchanged when only state/end/elapsed match, silently ignoring corrected CPU/GPU/user/partition/exit-code values. |
| medium | `jobwatch/reports.py` | 14, 65, 115 | Timestamp filtering and `MAX()` use lexicographic text comparison, which gives wrong chronological results for timezone-offset ISO strings. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py` | 110-114, 148-162 | Negative CPU and GPU allocations are accepted, allowing negative CPU/GPU-hour reports. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py` | 118-124 | Timezone-aware timestamps are accepted and stored without normalization, feeding inconsistent values into string-based report queries. |
| medium | `jobwatch/parser.py` | 153-156 | Empty user and partition values are accepted as valid records, creating unusable report group keys. |
| low | `jobwatch/cli.py` | 121-126, 138-143, 176-180 | Report commands create a new empty database when the path is wrong or missing, hiding operator mistakes. |
| low | `jobwatch/cli.py` | 25-37, 130-134, 145-168, 188-191 | Raw database fields are printed directly, so terminal escape/control sequences from input data can affect CLI output. |
| low | `jobwatch/db.py` | 13-27 | Schema has no versioning or migration path, which will make future active development risky once real databases exist. |

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **about 150 production lines**. That would cover safer upsert semantics, timestamp normalization/storage, input validation, missing-DB handling, output sanitization, and minimal schema migration support. Tests would also need updates beyond that.

issues.description: Same-rank terminal states overwrite each other without timestamp comparison, allowing stale dumps to replace newer final job data.
Rows are treated as unchanged when only state/end/elapsed match, so corrected CPU/GPU/user/partition/exit-code values are ignored.
Timestamp filtering and MAX() use lexicographic text comparison, producing wrong results for timezone-offset ISO strings.
Negative CPU and GPU allocations are accepted and can produce negative usage totals.
Timezone-aware timestamps are accepted but not normalized before storage and reporting.
Empty user and partition values are accepted as valid report grouping keys.
Report commands create a new empty database for a missing path, hiding operator mistakes.
Raw database fields are printed directly, allowing terminal escape/control sequences in CLI output.
SQLite schema has no versioning or migration path for future database changes.
